fact: Dayspring Law Firm states Cameroon's General Tax Code gives eligible innovative ICT start-ups a five-year full tax exemption then a further five years of reduced company tax (15%) and a 30% research tax credit.
system: General Tax Code innovative start-up incentives

fact: Dayspring Law Firm states start-ups must be approved by state-approved management centres, usually business incubators, before they can benefit from the tax incentives.

The Nkafu Policy Institute brief says Cameroon has not adopted a Startup Act but that a startup law has been in preparation since July 2021 at the Ministry in charge of Telecommunications, its elements not publicly available.
